extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, attorneys subject to USPTO disciplinary proceedings, and OED staff
extracted.subtask_description: A final order imposing reciprocal discipline (public reprimand) under USPTO regulations (37 C.F.R. § 11.24) based on a state-court public reprimand and describing service, response, publication, and notice requirements. Useful for practitioners facing USPTO discipline or for OED procedural reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal-discipline procedure under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director files a 'Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' requesting imposition of identical discipline, the respondent may contest imposition by filing a response within the time allowed; absent a timely response the Director may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact and impose identical discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order informed Respondent that if he seeks to contest imposition he shall file, within 40 days, a response containing all information he believes is sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact that imposition of identical discipline would be unwarranted based upon any of the grounds permissible under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1). The Director found Respondent did not file a response and accordingly determined 'there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)' and that a public reprimand was appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner violates 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) when he 'has been publicly reprimanded on ethical grounds by a duly constituted authority of' a state (here, Minnesota).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states Respondent is publicly reprimanded for violating § 10.23(b)(6) 'by having been publicly reprimanded on ethical grounds by a duly constituted authority of the State of Minnesota.' The Office may impose discipline based on such out-of-state disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-law professional-conduct violations supporting discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: State-court findings of violations of professional conduct rules (here, Minnesota Rules of Professional Conduct 3.3(a), 3.4(c), 4.4(a), and 8.4(d)) can support reciprocal discipline by the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice describes that the Minnesota Supreme Court publicly reprimanded Mr. Bunch for violating those specific rules. The reprimand was predicated on his representing in an affidavit that he would commence a civil action and then failing to timely commence it, which induced dismissal of a landlord-tenant action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and address requirements (37 C.F.R. § 11.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices in disciplinary proceedings must be mailed to the most recent address provided by the practitioner pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11; proper service starts response timelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order was mailed first-class certified mail, return receipt requested, to a street address in Plymouth, Minnesota (the most recent address provided under § 11.11). USPS tracking indicated delivery on August 22, 2011; Respondent did not file a response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response timeline and required content (40 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent has 40 days from mailing of the Notice and Order to file a response contesting imposition of identical discipline; the response must include all information sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order reiterates the 40-day deadline and that the response must identify grounds permissible under § 11.24(d)(1); failure to timely respond may result in the Office determining there is no genuine issue of material fact and imposing the requested discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notification requirements (37 C.F.R. § 11.59 and Official Gazette)
rubrics_metrics.description: When discipline is imposed, the OED Director shall publish the Final Order and a notice in the Official Gazette, and shall give notice of the public discipline and its reasons to state disciplinary agencies, courts where the practitioner is admitted, and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires the OED Director to publish this Final Order and to publish a NOTICE OF REPRIMAND in the Official Gazette. It also directs notice to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner is admitted, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and to the public; disciplinary decisions are posted in the OED Reading Room (URL provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory/legal authority for USPTO disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary action by the USPTO may be taken pursuant to statutory and regulatory authorities (here cited as 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order explicitly states 'This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59,' establishing the legal basis for the Office's reciprocal-discipline authority and publication/notice obligations.
